title: New York World’s Fair poster by Joseph Binder
lede: Joseph Binder’s poster for the 1939 fair: the Trylon and Perisphere in airbrushed light, with a streamlined train and liner on the horizon and slanted capitals.
summary: Trylon and Perisphere in searchlights over a red streamlined train and liner, with forward-slanting capitals. Joseph Binder, 1938–39.

source.label: Christie’s: Joseph Binder, New York World’s Fair 1939

made: 1938 (dated 20 July 1938 on Commons), for the 1939 fair

evidence.note: Downloaded and inspected the [Commons copy](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Joseph_Binder_New_York_World%27s_Fair_1939_The_World_of_Tomorrow.jpg), a scan from a Christie’s lot, at 1280 × 1939 px. I did not open the Christie’s page.

styles.note: Partial fit: the streamlined train and liner, the white speed swoosh, and the forward-slanting capitals are streamline; the vertical searchlight composition is Art Deco.
Late Art Deco poster: a monumental vertical axis, radiating searchlight beams, and airbrushed gradients on deep blue.

context: Poster for the 1939 New York World’s Fair, whose theme was “The World of Tomorrow”. The printer’s line reads “Made in U.S.A. by … Grinnell Litho. Co. Inc. N.Y.C.” (read on the scan). Commons dates the design 20 July 1938. [Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Joseph_Binder_New_York_World%27s_Fair_1939_The_World_of_Tomorrow.jpg).
observed: The ground is deep blue, lighter toward the bottom.
A tall yellow and white spire (the Trylon) rises at left of center beside a large glowing yellow-white sphere (the Perisphere) on a pale green-blue mound.
Pale blue searchlight beams cross the sky in diagonals; a formation of small red aircraft flies at upper left.
A white swoosh curls around the base of the sphere like a speed trail.
Along a red horizon line, a long streamlined red train runs left and a red ocean liner with rows of lit portholes sits at right; a skyline of lit windows rises at far left.
“NEW YORK WORLD’S FAIR” is set in white condensed sans-serif capitals that slant forward; “THE WORLD OF TOMORROW” and “1939” below are in pale blue.
The small line “© N.Y.W.F.” is printed at lower left.
interpretation: The poster places streamlined transport at the base of an Art Deco monument: the vertical beams belong to Deco, while the horizontal train, liner, and slanted capitals carry the streamline idea of speed. It fits the style record’s view of Streamline Moderne as a late branch of Art Deco.
borrow: Slant condensed capitals forward and let one line of them run the full width.
Draw a thin horizontal band of vehicles or shapes along a horizon line under a large calm field.

images.alt: Poster on deep blue: a tall yellow-white spire and a glowing sphere lit by crossing searchlights, red aircraft at upper left, a red streamlined train and ocean liner on the horizon, and the slanted words New York World's Fair, The World of Tomorrow, 1939.
images.caption: Joseph Binder, New York World’s Fair 1939. Scan from a Christie’s lot via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Joseph_Binder_New_York_World%27s_Fair_1939_The_World_of_Tomorrow.jpg), marked PD-US-not renewed.

rights.statement: Commons tags the scan PD-US-not renewed: the poster was first published in the United States (printed by Grinnell Litho, New York) and, per that tag, its copyright was not renewed. The poster carries a “© N.Y.W.F.” notice, so its public-domain status rests on non-renewal, which I did not check in the renewal records. Binder died in 1972; because the country of origin is the United States, the Austrian term does not apply. The lead curator should confirm or downgrade to tier D.
